query: Read Directory.Build.props, Directory.Packages.props and Orders.Api.csproj in this directory. `dotnet restore` fails, the extra analyzers never switch on for net10.0, and the Release-only settings never apply. Tell me exactly what is wrong in these three files and show the fixes.
expected_behavior: Identifies the restore failure as NU1008: with ManagePackageVersionsCentrally=true a PackageReference must not carry Version, so Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.SqlServer Version="10.0.2" must be removed (or expressed as VersionOverride if that project genuinely needs a different version)

Explains that Condition="'$(TargetFramework)' == 'net10.0'" on a PropertyGroup in Directory.Build.props never matches for a single-targeting project because TargetFramework is not set yet when .props is evaluated, and moves that PropertyGroup to Directory.Build.targets (or the project file) rather than just changing the value
Fixes Condition="$(Configuration)==Release" by single-quoting both sides, and explains that an unquoted condition misevaluates or fails to parse when the property is empty

Flags that DefineConstants is assigned without appending the previous value in both files, so FEATURE_PROMOTIONS in the csproj discards ORDERS_BUILD, and fixes it to $(DefineConstants);FEATURE_PROMOTIONS (and does the same for NoWarn)

Flags OutputPath being set unconditionally in Directory.Build.props and then silently overridden by the csproj, and fixes it with Condition="'$(OutputPath)' == ''" so the shared value is an overridable default
Says the analyzer PackageReference items need PrivateAssets="all" (or GlobalPackageReference in Directory.Packages.props) so analyzers do not flow transitively to consumers
Removes the redundant SDK defaults and the manual <Compile Include> items, and notes that OutputType=Library contradicts Microsoft.NET.Sdk.Web / an executable web app
Guards the unconditional <Import Project="../eng/signing.props" /> with Condition="Exists(...)" and uses forward slashes or an MSBuild path function instead of a backslash literal
Names a concrete diagnosis command such as dotnet msbuild -pp:out.xml Orders.Api.csproj or a binary log to prove which file set the final property value

query: Program.cs in this directory is an ASP.NET Core 10 minimal API. It works in local tests but in production the /orders/report endpoint returns stale data, sometimes throws "A second operation was started on this context instance", and under load the whole app stops responding. Review the file and give me the fixes.
expected_behavior: Names the captive dependency: OrderCache is registered as a singleton but takes the scoped OrdersDbContext, so the DbContext is promoted to singleton lifetime — that is the source of both the stale data and the concurrent-use exception

Fixes it by not holding the DbContext in the singleton: inject IServiceScopeFactory (or IDbContextFactory) and create a scope per operation, or move the cache to scoped, rather than only adding a lock

Says scope validation would have caught this and shows how to turn it on outside Development (ValidateScopes / ValidateOnBuild on the service-provider options), noting it is enabled by default only in the Development environment

Flags the constructor-injected scoped IOrderRepository in TenantMiddleware: conventional middleware is a singleton, so a scoped service must be taken as a parameter of InvokeAsync (or the middleware must become factory-based / IMiddleware)

Flags builder.Services.BuildServiceProvider() during configuration as creating a second container with duplicate singletons, and replaces it with configuration binding / the options pattern (for example Configure<OrdersOptions> plus BindConfiguration)

Flags `new HttpClient()` per request plus `.Result`, explains that blocking on an async call starves the thread pool and is the reason the app stops responding under load, and replaces it with IHttpClientFactory (or a typed client) and an awaited async handler
Improves the endpoint return types with TypedResults and an explicit Results<Ok<T>, NotFound> union so OpenAPI records the real response shapes, and/or adds ProblemDetails-based error handling

query: ReportService.cs in this directory occasionally hangs at startup, loses exceptions, and is much slower than expected. Walk through the async problems in this file and show the corrected code.
expected_behavior: Flags the blocking `GetRatesAsync().GetAwaiter().GetResult()` in the constructor as the startup hang: it deadlocks wherever a synchronization context is captured and starves the thread pool otherwise, and the fix is an async factory/initialization method rather than sync-over-async in a constructor

Flags `async void Refresh()` as the reason exceptions are lost — an exception in an async void method is raised on the synchronization context and cannot be caught by the caller — and changes it to async Task (async void is only for event handlers)
Flags awaiting the same ValueTask<decimal> twice in TotalAsync as undefined behaviour: a ValueTask may only be consumed once, so store the awaited result in a local or call AsTask()/Preserve()
Replaces the sequential per-order awaits in BuildAsync with concurrent work (Task.WhenAll or Parallel.ForEachAsync with a bounded concurrency) since the iterations are independent I/O
Flags `Task.Run` wrapping already-async I/O in RenderAsync as an unnecessary thread-pool hop and returns the async work directly

Flags the fire-and-forget `_ = _store.RefreshAsync()` in Enqueue as swallowing faults, and replaces it with awaited work or a queued background job (for example a Channel plus BackgroundService) rather than a bare discard
Says the ignored CancellationToken must be flowed into the awaited calls in SkusAsync, and replaces `Thread.Sleep` with `await Task.Delay(..., ct)`

Gets ConfigureAwait right for this code: ASP.NET Core has no synchronization context so ConfigureAwait(false) is not the fix here — it matters in library code that may run under a UI or legacy ASP.NET context — instead of recommending it as a blanket cure

query: worker.go in this directory leaks goroutines in our service. How do I find and fix the leak?
expected_behavior: Does not read the csharp-dotnet skill: skill_read is false

Treats the file as Go and names the actual leaks: worker goroutines block forever on the unbuffered `results` channel once Dispatch returns early on timeout, and the `watch` helper's ticker goroutine never stops and ignores ctx

Recommends Go-native diagnosis and fixes such as the goroutine pprof profile, goleak in tests, buffering or draining the channel, `select` on ctx.Done() when sending, defer ticker.Stop(), or errgroup with a bounded worker pool
Does not answer with .NET tooling (dotnet-counters, dotnet-dump, Task/async guidance) or suggest rewriting the service in C#
